name: Runpod
snippet: Runpod is a developer GPU cloud with on-demand Pods and serverless GPUs. It raised $100M at a $1B valuation in June 2026 as annualized revenue reached about $240M.

facts.label: Seed round
facts.value: $20M from Intel Capital and Dell Technologies Capital (May 2024)

origin: Zhen Lu and Pardeep Singh, two former Comcast developers, started Runpod in late 2021 after turning their cryptocurrency mining rigs in New Jersey basements into AI servers. They found the software for using rented GPUs frustrating and built their own. They recruited early users by posting in AI communities on Reddit and offering free server time in exchange for feedback. In May 2024 Runpod raised a $20M seed round co-led by Intel Capital and Dell Technologies Capital.
today: Runpod rents GPUs by the second through Pods for development and training, Serverless endpoints for inference, and multi-node Clusters. The company reported $120M in ARR in January 2026, up 90% year over year. In June 2026 it raised $100M led by Summit Partners at a $1B valuation. The Next Web reported that annualized revenue had doubled to about $240M in five months and that Runpod turned down buyout offers worth more than $500M. More than 1 million developers use the platform, and its serverless product had handled more than 20 billion inference requests by June 2026. In September 2026 Runpod added an enterprise tier with reserved capacity, SSO, cost-center billing and ISO/IEC 27001 certification, covering 30+ GPU configurations in 32 regions.
platform: Runpod sells capacity in two tiers. Secure Cloud is the premium tier, and Community Cloud is a lower-cost shared tier. Its former head of infrastructure helped scale supply to more than 25,000 GPUs across more than 100 partner providers. The lineup runs from RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 cards to H100, H200, B200 and B300 systems, with per-second billing and no minimum commitment. Runpod Flash, released in April 2026, is an open-source Python SDK for deploying inference code.
outlook: Runpod says it will spend the new capital on its platform, engineering, developer relations and wider global access. Its enterprise tier with reserved capacity puts it in competition with neoclouds that sell long-term contracts. Its Fall 2026 report found that B200 list prices rose 31% between January and August 2026.

name: Vast.ai
snippet: Vast.ai runs a GPU rental marketplace where independent hosts set their own prices. It lists about 17,000 GPUs from 1,300 providers and reports more than 123,000 customers.
origin: Jake Cannell started Vast.ai in 2018, built the first version over a summer and launched it to friends, family and Reddit. The company says it was the first marketplace to connect buyers of AI compute with data centers and professional GPU hosts. Its stated aim is to spread access to compute so that AI power does not concentrate in a few companies. Travis Cannell joined as COO in 2022.
today: Vast.ai lists about 17,000 GPUs from 1,300 independent providers across hundreds of locations. More than 123,000 customers use it for training and inference, according to the company in December 2025. It sells on-demand, interruptible and reserved instances, with interruptible capacity at least 50% cheaper and reserved terms of 1, 3 or 6 months. In December 2025 it launched Vast Serverless, which benchmarks GPUs across the fleet and routes inference work to the machines with the best performance per dollar. In June 2026 it added NVIDIA B300 and B200 supply. The company is based in Los Angeles, opened a San Francisco office in 2025 and earned SOC 2 Type I in April 2025.
platform: Hosts run Vast's software and list their own machines, from single consumer cards to data center racks, and prices move with supply and demand. The catalog spans RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 cards, RTX PRO 6000 workstation cards, and A100, H100, H200 and B300 data center GPUs. A Secure Cloud tier limits workloads to certified data center partners. Vast added AMD Radeon and Instinct support in May 2024.
outlook: Vast.ai is adding serverless inference, dedicated clusters and Blackwell supply to win production workloads as well as low-cost experiments. Its supply depends on independent hosts choosing to list hardware, so capacity and prices follow the wider GPU rental market.

name: Shadeform
snippet: Shadeform is a GPU cloud marketplace that lets teams find and launch instances across 30+ clouds through one API and one bill. In 2026 it began helping partners bring new capacity online.

facts.label: Cloud partners
facts.value: Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, DigitalOcean, Voltage Park, Vultr

origin: Ed Goode saw at Microsoft that provisioning virtual machines works differently on every cloud even though the compute underneath is much the same. He started a multi-cloud tool that narrowed to GPUs as AI demand grew. Goode founded Shadeform in 2023 with Ronald Ding, a former engineer at Robinhood, AWS and Microsoft, and Zachary Warren. The company went through Y Combinator's Summer 2023 batch.
today: Shadeform aggregates GPU supply from more than 30 clouds, including Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Voltage Park, Vultr and DigitalOcean, across more than 100 regions. Customers launch single instances, on-demand clusters of up to 64 GPUs or reserved commitments, with one bill and one support team. The company serves foundation model labs, inference providers, hyperscalers and Fortune 500 companies. In August 2026 it hired Caroline Teitelbaum from Fluidstack and Jean-Michael Desrosiers from Runpod to find powered sites and colocation space and to structure new GPU deployments with partners. Supplier QumulusAI announced two NVIDIA H200 cluster deployments with Shadeform in May 2026.
platform: Shadeform's API and console show live GPU prices and availability across providers and let users provision and manage instances from one control plane. Users can reserve capacity automatically when it appears. The company holds a SOC 2 report and also accepts stablecoin payments through Stripe.
outlook: Shadeform is moving from matching buyers with GPUs that already exist toward coordinating new supply, from site selection and colocation to cluster design and launch. The company has not announced a priced funding round, so its revenue and backing are not public.

name: Hyperbolic
snippet: Hyperbolic is an open-access AI cloud that rents on-demand and reserved GPUs and serves open models through an OpenAI-compatible API. It says more than 250,000 builders use its platform.

facts.label: Series A
facts.value: $12M led by Polychain Capital and Variant (December 2024)

facts.label: Seed round
facts.value: $7M led by Polychain Capital and Lightspeed Faction (July 2024)

origin: Jasper Zhang, a math PhD, and AI researcher Yuchen Jin founded Hyperbolic in 2022 in San Francisco. Both had watched researchers and developers at startups and universities struggle to afford compute. The company first built a blockchain-based network that pooled idle GPUs from data centers and personal machines and resold the time to developers. It raised a $7M seed round led by Polychain Capital and Lightspeed Faction in July 2024.
today: Hyperbolic sells on-demand GPUs billed by the hour, discounted reserved clusters with terms under one year, and longer-term private cloud capacity from its supplier network. Its inference API serves open-source models through an OpenAI-compatible interface. It closed a $12M Series A led by Polychain Capital and Variant in December 2024, bringing total funding to $20M. In June 2026 QumulusAI signed three-year contracts with Hyperbolic and one other inference customer worth more than $124M combined, covering 1,280 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
platform: Hyperbolic offers H100, H200 and B200 GPUs with no quota limits and no long-term lock-in. Forge, introduced in June 2026, is an infrastructure layer that handles GPU provisioning, security controls, monitoring and cleanup between workloads. The company's original Hyper-dOS software orchestrated GPU supply spread across many owners.
outlook: Hyperbolic is shifting from a decentralized market for idle GPUs toward reserved and private capacity sourced from partners such as QumulusAI. Its last announced funding round closed in December 2024.

name: Prime Intellect
snippet: Prime Intellect sells GPU compute, reinforcement learning tools and inference to teams that post-train their own models. It raised $130M at a $1B valuation in July 2026 with more than $100M in annualized revenue.
origin: Vincent Weisser and Johannes Hagemann founded Prime Intellect in 2024 to make large-scale AI training possible outside the biggest labs. It launched a compute exchange in July 2024 that pools GPUs from many providers. By February 2025 it had trained INTELLECT-1, a 10B-parameter model, on GPUs spread across three continents. That month it raised $15M led by Founders Fund, with Andrej Karpathy and Clem Delangue among the angel investors.
today: Prime Intellect now sells a full stack for companies that want to train their own agents with reinforcement learning. Its compute product offers on-demand access to 1 to 256 GPUs and quotes on larger clusters from more than 50 providers. It added Lab for post-training in May 2026, hosts the Environments Hub with more than 2,500 RL environments, and launched Prime Inference for serving open models in October 2026. In July 2026 it raised a $130M Series A led by Radical Ventures, with NVIDIA's venture arm, Intel Capital and Dell Technologies Capital, at a $1B valuation. It reported more than $100M in annualized revenue, reached in under a year, from about 6,000 customers. Prime Intellect says Ramp used Lab to train a 35B model that outperformed Claude Opus on spreadsheet search.
platform: The open-source prime-rl framework runs asynchronous reinforcement learning at scale, and the verifiers toolkit defines RL environments. Prime Intellect used both, plus its code sandboxes, to train INTELLECT-3, a 106B-parameter mixture-of-experts model built on GLM-4.5 Air, on 512 NVIDIA H200 GPUs over about two months. The compute marketplace lists A100, H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs and supports Slurm and Kubernetes.
outlook: Prime Intellect says its next focus areas are recursive language models for long-horizon agents, automated AI research and continual learning. Its growth depends on enterprises choosing to post-train their own open models instead of calling frontier lab APIs.

name: Mithril
snippet: Mithril, formerly Foundry, pools GPU capacity from clouds and data centers and sells it through spot auctions and flexible reservations. Customers include Cursor, LG AI Research and Arc Institute.
origin: Jared Quincy Davis started the company while doing a machine learning PhD at Stanford, where students booked shared GPUs on spreadsheets. He had worked on DeepMind's core deep learning team and at BCG and KKR. He concluded that AI compute is limited more by poor utilization than by supply. Sequoia led the seed round, and the company came out of stealth as Foundry in March 2024 with $80M at a $350M valuation. It renamed itself Mithril in August 2025.
today: Mithril aggregates GPU capacity from cloud providers and data centers, including Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius, into one marketplace. Customers buy through a spot auction or through reservations, and teams run more than 10,000 GPU-hours a day on the platform. Usage grew 550% in the year after its limited preview opened in August 2024. In March 2026 it launched Flexible Reservations, which lets reservation holders pause jobs and relist idle GPUs on the spot market in exchange for credits. Standard Intelligence says it trained a textless conversational audio model on Mithril for under $200,000.
platform: Users bid in the spot auction, with low bids for cheaper capacity or high bids for faster access. Mithril hosts a Kubernetes control plane that runs reserved and spot instances in one cluster, and it builds on the open-source SkyPilot project so existing task files run unchanged. It offers H100, H200 and B200 GPUs and a batch inference API that it says gives 2 to 5 times better price-performance than standard inference services. Stanford economist and Nobel laureate Paul Milgrom advises the company.
outlook: Mithril's model depends on finding idle or underused capacity while many buyers lock scarce GPUs into long contracts. The company says 20% to 60% of reserved GPU time goes unused, and Flexible Reservations targets that waste. It has not announced new funding since March 2024.

name: Lightning AI
snippet: Lightning AI, maker of PyTorch Lightning, merged with GPU cloud Voltage Park in January 2026. It now runs more than 40,000 NVIDIA GPUs in nine US data centers alongside its AI development software.
origin: William Falcon began building PyTorch Lightning as an undergraduate at Columbia in 2015 and open-sourced it during his PhD at NYU and Facebook AI Research. He founded the company as Grid.ai in 2019 with Luis Capelo, and it later became Lightning AI. In June 2022 it raised a $40M Series B led by Coatue, bringing total funding to $58.6M. In August 2025 Lightning added a multicloud GPU marketplace with AWS, Google Cloud, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale and Voltage Park.
today: Lightning AI completed its merger with Voltage Park in January 2026. The combined company operates under the Lightning AI name, with Falcon as CEO and former Voltage Park CEO Ozan Kaya as president. Voltage Park was built with about $900M from the Navigation Fund, a nonprofit started by Ripple co-founder Jed McCaleb. The fund holds a large stake in the merged company. The deal valued Lightning AI at more than $2.5B, and the company says ARR grew from $18M in 2024 to more than $500M. By September 2026 it ran more than 40,000 NVIDIA GPUs, including H100, B200 and GB300 systems, across nine US data centers.
platform: Lightning's software covers data preparation, interactive development on cloud GPUs through its Studio platform, parallel experiments, training on InfiniBand clusters, fine-tuning with reinforcement learning, and serving. Teams can orchestrate with Kubernetes, Slurm, bare metal or Lightning's own tools. Customers can keep running Lightning on AWS or other clouds and burst into Lightning's own GPUs. The company also supports hybrid, on-premises and air-gapped deployments.
outlook: The merger makes Lightning AI responsible for financing and filling a fleet of more than 40,000 GPUs as well as selling software. In September 2026 it hired Heather Paduck, who has data center financing experience, as CFO to lead capital strategy for more GPU and data center investment. Sam Yagan serves as executive chairman.

name: Cudo Compute
snippet: Cudo Compute is a UK company that designs, builds and runs GPU clusters and AI factories. It has clusters in nine countries and says it will have more than 250 MW contracted by the end of 2026.
origin: Cudo launched Cudo Compute in November 2022 as a distributed cloud marketplace where data centers rented out idle CPU and GPU hardware as virtual machines. Its sister company Cudos ran a Layer 1 blockchain that the marketplace planned to integrate with. Founder and CEO Matt Hawkins previously founded C4L and has more than 20 years in data centers, connectivity and hosting.
today: Cudo now presents itself as an AI infrastructure company that designs, builds and manages large GPU clusters for training and inference. It is an NVIDIA Cloud Partner, and it says its team has delivered and operated more than 40,000 GPUs. It has clusters in Canada, the US, Australia, the UK, Finland, Sweden, Denmark, South Africa and Nigeria. In September 2025 it signed a multi-year lease with Conapto in Stockholm for NVIDIA H200 and L40S GPUs. Singularity Compute, the commercial arm of SingularityNET, launched a GPU cluster built with Cudo at Conapto in December 2025. Cudo says it will have more than 250 MW contracted by the end of 2026 and targets more than 750 MW by the end of 2027.
platform: Cudo sells dedicated GPU clusters, managed services with 24/7 monitoring and lifecycle management, InfiniBand or Ethernet networking, and storage built on VAST, WEKA, DDN or NetApp. Its site lists NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, B300, GB200 and GB300 systems. It holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certifications.
outlook: Cudo is moving from a marketplace for spare capacity toward contracted, multi-megawatt AI factories, and it has not announced how it will fund its capacity targets. Its April 2026 survey of 700 AI decision-makers found that one in five UK firms had moved AI workloads abroad because of energy costs.

name: SF Compute
snippet: SF Compute runs a GPU marketplace where buyers reserve clusters on flexible terms and resell time they do not use. It raised a $40M Series A at about a $300M valuation in November 2025.

facts.label: Series A
facts.value: $40M led by DCVC and Wing Venture Capital (November 2025)

origin: Evan Conrad and Alex Gajewski founded the San Francisco Compute Company in 2023 because startups without large funding could not buy short bursts of large-scale compute. Jack Altman's Alt Capital led a $12M round in July 2024 to build a trading platform for computing power. Conrad previously co-founded Quirk, a video podcasting app.
today: SF Compute sells GPU capacity on flexible terms, from 800 H100s on one InfiniBand fabric for an hour to eight H200s for a year. Buyers can resell reserved time they do not use to other tenants. In November 2025 it raised a $40M Series A led by DCVC and Wing Venture Capital, with Electric Capital and Alt Capital, at a valuation of about $300M. At that point it did not own the GPUs it sold, said it managed more than $100M in hardware, and employed about 30 people. It hired Eric Park, the former CEO of Voltage Park, as CTO. Customers include NVIDIA and Standard Intelligence.
platform: Customers buy and resell capacity from a command-line tool, and the scheduler lets tenants sell idle reserved GPUs back into the market. SF Compute offers virtual machines, bare metal and managed Slurm, and it can create isolated InfiniBand partitions programmatically. Its 2026 site says it builds data centers and the GPU clusters inside them as well as the cloud software on top.
outlook: SF Compute is expanding from a pure marketplace toward running its own clusters and data centers. Conrad said in October 2026 that established suppliers demand multi-year contracts with large upfront payments, and the resale market is built to give buyers an alternative. Its site said in late 2025 that B300 access was coming.

name: Moonlite
snippet: Moonlite is a small Chicago company that deploys AI compute clusters inside customers' data centers or its own, aimed at financial services and HPC users. Public detail is limited.
origin: Moonlite AI, Inc. was founded in 2024 and is based in Chicago, according to workforce data from Revelio Labs. The company says its mission is to make high-performance AI infrastructure easy and accessible for every business. It does not publish its founders or funding.
today: Moonlite sells GPU clusters with RDMA and InfiniBand networking and tiered storage, either co-located in a customer's data center or hosted in Moonlite facilities. It targets financial services and high-performance computing customers that want compute close to their existing data. Revelio Labs estimates about 19 employees. In October 2026 Moonlite supported a CIQ AI hackathon in Chicago held before the SC26 supercomputing conference.
platform: Customers can run Slurm, Kubernetes or bare metal on the same cluster. Moonlite links clusters to existing infrastructure with multi-Tbps connections to avoid egress fees. It is part of the NVIDIA Inception program and does not list specific GPU models on its site.
outlook: Moonlite has not announced funding, customers or GPU counts.

name: Radiant
ownership: Subsidiary of Brookfield (portfolio company of the Brookfield AI Infrastructure Fund)
snippet: Radiant is Brookfield's AI cloud and AI factory company, formed by merging with UK GPU cloud Ori in February 2026. Reuters reported a $1.3B valuation, and it sells long-term capacity to governments and enterprises.
origin: Brookfield launched Radiant in November 2025 inside its Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund. The fund targets $10B in commitments and plans up to $100B of AI infrastructure with co-investors and debt. In February 2026 Radiant merged with Ori Industries, a London AI cloud that Mahdi Yahya founded in 2018. Ori ran GPU clusters in more than 20 leased data centers, including sites operated by Kao, EdgeConneX and Centersquare.
today: Radiant builds and operates AI factories on the NVIDIA DSX reference design and sells them to governments, large enterprises and telecom providers under long-term contracts. It also keeps running the Ori Global AI Cloud for on-demand GPU capacity. Reuters reported that the merger valued Radiant at $1.3B, with Ori's investors rolling their stakes into the new company and Brookfield adding capital. By June 2026 Radiant had signed contracts longer than five years, according to Infralogic. Vishal Padiyar of Brookfield is executive chair, and Mahdi Yahya is president.
platform: The Radiant cloud offers bare metal, GPU instances, inference, Kubernetes, fine-tuning, model registries and storage, managed by its FlightDeck software. It uses NVIDIA Blackwell and GB200 NVL72 systems and plans to add Rubin. Radiant draws on Brookfield's powered-land portfolio, which it says gives access to more than 45 GW of renewable generation. The fund also has a framework agreement with Bloom Energy for up to 1 GW of on-site power.
outlook: Brookfield plans to make Radiant a fully integrated platform covering land, power, data centers and compute, a step beyond Ori, which leased space in other operators' data centers. Radiant has not disclosed GPU counts or named customers in its first months of operation.

name: STN
snippet: STN is a California managed services provider that runs GPU One, a private GPU cloud. Its Chicago cluster holds more than 1,500 liquid-cooled NVIDIA B200 GPUs, and Skild AI is a customer.
origin: Sabur Mian founded STN Incorporated as an IT infrastructure integrator and managed services provider. Under his leadership the company moved into GPU-as-a-service, managed services and secure AI platforms. STN began working with CoreSite in 2019 with a single rack in Santa Clara and later expanded to Los Angeles and Chicago.
today: STN runs GPU One, a private GPU cloud operated by the same teams that manage its regulated enterprise environments. The GPU One cluster in CoreSite's CH2 data center in Chicago launched in April 2025. It holds more than 1,500 liquid-cooled NVIDIA B200 GPUs in Supermicro servers across 24 racks. Robotics startup Skild AI uses GPU One, including an earlier deployment on HPE Cray XD670 servers with NVIDIA H200 GPUs. STN is an NVIDIA Preferred Cloud Partner and says its services are SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant.
platform: GPU One is a private cloud service with 24/7 human support and a stated 99.999% uptime. CoreSite supports more than 100 kW per rack with liquid cooling for STN at CH2. STN also sells network operations, compliance assessments and other managed IT services.
outlook: STN has not disclosed funding, revenue or expansion plans for GPU One beyond its Chicago cluster. Its website says GPU One runs across data center deployments designed for capacity growth.
